source_caption:
Long before audiences knew him as Tyrion Lannister in Game of Thrones, Peter Dinklage delivered one of his finest performances in 𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐒𝐭𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧 𝐀𝐠𝐞𝐧𝐭 (𝟐𝟎𝟎𝟑), a small independent film that proves you don’t need a complicated plot to tell a great story.⁣
⁣
Written and directed by Thomas McCarthy, the film follows Finbar McBride (Dinklage), a quiet man with a passion for trains who has spent much of his life avoiding attention. When his only friend dies and leaves him an abandoned railway depot in rural New Jersey, Fin moves there hoping to finally live in peace, away from the constant staring and unwanted attention he has endured because of his dwarfism.⁣
⁣
What makes this movie so special is how naturally the characters develop. McCarthy allows his characters to reveal themselves through ordinary conversations, awkward encounters and moments of silence.  At just 88 minutes, The Station Agent (2003) is a film that somehow feels too short, not because anything is missing, but because you genuinely want to spend more time with these characters.⁣
⁣

source_details.title: The Station Agent
source_details.synopsis: The Station Agent is a 2003 American comedy-drama film written and directed by Tom McCarthy in his directorial debut. It stars Peter Dinklage as a man who seeks solitude in an abandoned train station in the Newfoundland section of Jefferson Township, New Jersey. It also stars Patricia Clarkson, Bobby Cannavale, Raven Goodwin, Paul Benjamin, Michelle Williams and John Slattery. For his writing achievement, McCarthy won the BAFTA Award for Best Original Screenplay, the Independent Spirit Award for Best First Screenplay and the Waldo Salt Screenwriting Award. The film itself also won the John Cassavetes Award.
